_about: Events the Theographic data does not carry. It has almost nothing between Solomon and the Gospels apart from reigns and prophets, so most of the Divided Kingdom, the Exile and the Return are written here, with a few from Genesis to Samuel and after Acts 28. `tier`: 1 headline, 2 main, 3 detail. `parent` is another item's id (tg-<eventID> for a Theographic event). People and places are People-pack and Theographic place ids.

events.title: Abraham offers Isaac
events.summary: God tests Abraham on Mount Moriah and provides the ram in Isaac's place: 'The LORD will provide.'

events.title: Jacob's dream at Bethel
events.summary: Fleeing Esau, Jacob sees a ladder to heaven and receives the promise given to Abraham and Isaac.

events.title: Jacob wrestles with God
events.summary: At the Jabbok Jacob wrestles until daybreak and is renamed Israel.

events.title: Jacob's family moves to Egypt
events.summary: Seventy of Jacob's household go down to Joseph and settle in Goshen; the 430 years in Egypt begin.

events.title: A new Pharaoh enslaves Israel
events.summary: A king who did not know Joseph sets taskmasters over Israel to build Pithom and Rameses, then orders the boys thrown into the Nile.

events.title: The burning bush
events.summary: God calls Moses from a bush that burns and is not consumed, and gives his name: I AM WHO I AM.

events.title: Crossing the Red Sea
events.summary: The sea parts for Israel and closes over Pharaoh's chariots; Moses and Miriam sing.

events.title: Manna from heaven
events.summary: Bread from heaven every morning but the Sabbath, for forty years.

events.title: The golden calf
events.summary: While Moses is on the mountain, Aaron makes a calf of gold; Moses breaks the tablets and pleads for the people.

events.title: The twelve spies and the refusal at Kadesh
events.summary: Ten spies say the land cannot be taken, and the people refuse to go in; that generation will die in the wilderness.

events.title: The bronze serpent
events.summary: Whoever looked at the serpent Moses lifted up lived; Jesus said the Son of Man must be lifted up the same way.

events.title: Balaam blesses Israel
events.summary: Hired to curse Israel, Balaam can only bless it, and foretells a star out of Jacob.

events.title: Moses' farewell on the plains of Moab
events.summary: Moses retells the Law to the new generation: hear, O Israel; choose life.

events.title: The walls of Jericho fall
events.summary: Seven days around the city, and the walls fall flat; only Rahab's house is spared.

events.title: The sun stands still at Gibeon
events.summary: Five Amorite kings defeated in one long day.

events.title: 'As for me and my house'
events.summary: Joshua gathers the tribes at Shechem to renew the covenant before he dies.

events.title: Ruth and Boaz
events.summary: A Moabite widow follows Naomi to Bethlehem and marries Boaz; she becomes David's great-grandmother.

events.title: Hannah's prayer and Samuel's birth
events.summary: Hannah prays for a son and gives him back to the LORD at Shiloh.

events.title: The LORD calls Samuel
events.summary: 'Speak, for your servant hears.' Samuel becomes a prophet to all Israel.

events.title: Victory at Mizpah: Ebenezer
events.summary: Israel puts away its idols and the Philistines are routed: 'Till now the LORD has helped us.'

events.title: Israel asks for a king
events.summary: The elders want a king like all the nations; God tells Samuel it is him they have rejected.

events.title: Saul anointed king
events.summary: Samuel anoints Saul of Benjamin, and after his victory at Jabesh-gilead he is made king at Gilgal.

events.title: Samuel anoints David
events.summary: The youngest son of Jesse, keeping the sheep: man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.

events.title: David on the run from Saul
events.summary: Years in caves and among the Philistines; twice David spares the king who is hunting him.

events.title: David king over Judah at Hebron
events.summary: After Saul's death the men of Judah anoint David; the other tribes follow Saul's son Ish-bosheth for seven years.

events.title: David king over all Israel; Jerusalem taken
events.summary: All the tribes come to Hebron to make David king, and he takes the Jebusite stronghold of Zion for his capital.

events.title: The ark brought to Jerusalem
events.summary: David dances before the LORD with all his might as the ark comes up to the city of David.

events.title: God's covenant with David
events.summary: David wants to build God a house; God promises instead to build David a house, and a throne established forever.

events.title: David and Bathsheba
events.summary: Adultery and the murder of Uriah, then Nathan's parable and David's repentance.

events.title: Absalom's revolt
events.summary: David's son steals the hearts of Israel and drives his father from Jerusalem; 'O Absalom, my son, my son!'

events.title: Solomon crowned; he asks for wisdom
events.summary: Anointed at Gihon before David dies; at Gibeon he asks for an understanding heart and is given riches and honour besides.

events.title: The Temple dedicated
events.summary: The ark is brought into the Most Holy Place and the glory of the LORD fills the house.

events.title: The queen of Sheba visits
events.summary: She came to test Solomon with hard questions, and found that not the half had been told her.

events.title: The kingdom divides
events.summary: Rehoboam answers harshly at Shechem and ten tribes make Jeroboam king; only Judah and Benjamin stay with David's house.

events.title: Golden calves at Bethel and Dan
events.summary: 'Behold your gods, O Israel': the sin of Jeroboam that every northern king would follow.

events.title: Shishak plunders Jerusalem
events.summary: Pharaoh carries off the treasures of the Temple and Solomon's shields of gold.

events.title: Omri builds Samaria
events.summary: Omri buys the hill of Samaria for two talents of silver and makes it Israel's capital.

events.title: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath
events.summary: Elijah shuts the sky, is fed by ravens, and raises a widow's son.

events.title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
events.summary: Fire falls on Elijah's soaked altar and the prophets of Baal are defeated: 'The LORD, he is God.'

events.title: Elijah at Horeb: the still small voice
events.summary: Running from Jezebel, Elijah hears God not in the wind, earthquake or fire, but in a low whisper.

events.title: Naboth's vineyard
events.summary: Jezebel has Naboth stoned so Ahab can take his vineyard; Elijah meets Ahab there with God's sentence.

events.title: Naaman healed
events.summary: The Syrian commander dips seven times in the Jordan and his skin is made like a child's.

events.title: Jehu wipes out the house of Ahab
events.summary: Anointed in secret, Jehu drives furiously to Jezreel; Joram, Ahaziah and Jezebel die, then the prophets of Baal.

events.title: Joash repairs the Temple
events.summary: A chest with a hole in its lid by the altar, and the money given gladly for the work.

events.title: Death of Elisha
events.summary: On his deathbed he tells the king to strike the ground; even his bones bring a dead man back to life.

events.title: Jonah preaches at Nineveh
events.summary: After three days in the fish, Jonah preaches and the great city repents, to his anger.

events.title: Isaiah sees the Lord
events.summary: In the year King Uzziah died: 'Holy, holy, holy', a coal on his lips, and 'Here am I, send me.'

events.title: The sign of Immanuel
events.summary: Ahaz will not ask for a sign, so God gives one: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son.

events.title: Galilee carried off to Assyria
events.summary: The first deportation from the north, and Isaiah's promise that the people who walked in darkness would see a great light.

events.title: Samaria falls; Israel exiled to Assyria
events.summary: After a three-year siege the northern kingdom ends; its people are scattered across Assyria and foreigners settle the land.

events.title: Hezekiah's reform and Passover
events.summary: The Temple cleansed, the bronze serpent broken up, and a Passover like none since Solomon.

events.title: Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem
events.summary: Assyria takes every fortified city but one; Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD, and 185,000 die in a night.

events.title: Hezekiah's illness: fifteen more years
events.summary: Told to set his house in order, Hezekiah weeps and prays; the shadow goes back ten steps.

events.title: Envoys from Babylon
events.summary: Hezekiah shows them all his treasures, and Isaiah says it will all be carried to Babylon.

events.title: Manasseh taken to Babylon, and repents
events.summary: Led away with hooks and bronze chains, the worst of Judah's kings humbles himself and is restored.

events.title: Jeremiah called
events.summary: 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you'; a young priest from Anathoth is sent to the nations.

events.title: The Book of the Law found; Josiah's reform
events.summary: Repairing the Temple, the priests find the Law; Josiah tears his clothes, renews the covenant and purges the land.

events.title: Nineveh falls
events.summary: Babylon and the Medes destroy Assyria's capital, as Nahum foretold.

events.title: Josiah killed at Megiddo
events.summary: Josiah goes out against Pharaoh Neco and is shot by archers; Jeremiah writes a lament for him.

events.title: Babylon defeats Egypt at Carchemish
events.summary: The battle that made Babylon master of the whole region, Judah included.

events.title: Daniel and the first exiles taken to Babylon
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes young nobles to be trained for his court; Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king's food.

events.title: Jehoiakim burns Jeremiah's scroll
events.summary: He cuts it up a few columns at a time and throws it on the fire; Jeremiah dictates it all again, with more.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the statue
events.summary: Gold, silver, bronze, iron and clay: four kingdoms, and a stone not cut by hands that fills the earth.

events.title: Jehoiachin and ten thousand taken to Babylon
events.summary: The second deportation: the king, his court, the craftsmen, and a young priest named Ezekiel.

events.title: Ezekiel's vision by the Chebar
events.summary: Wheels within wheels and the likeness of the glory of the LORD, among the exiles in Babylonia.

events.title: The fiery furnace
events.summary: Three young men will not bow to the golden image, and a fourth walks with them in the fire.

events.title: Jerusalem and the Temple destroyed
events.summary: After an eighteen-month siege Babylon breaks through the walls, burns Solomon's Temple, and carries the people into exile.

events.title: Gedaliah murdered; the remnant flees to Egypt
events.summary: The governor Babylon left is assassinated, and the survivors take Jeremiah with them to Egypt against his word.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar humbled
events.summary: Driven out to eat grass like an ox until he knows that the Most High rules the kingdom of men.

events.title: Jehoiachin released from prison
events.summary: The book of Kings ends with David's heir eating at the king of Babylon's table: the line still lives.

events.title: The writing on the wall; Babylon falls
events.summary: Mene, mene, tekel, parsin: that night Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians.

events.title: Daniel in the lions' den
events.summary: Daniel keeps praying toward Jerusalem three times a day, and God shuts the lions' mouths.

events.title: Cyrus's decree: the first return
events.summary: Seventy years after Daniel was taken, Cyrus sends the exiles home with the Temple vessels; about 50,000 return under Zerubbabel.

events.title: The Temple's foundation laid
events.summary: Shouts of joy, and the old men who had seen the first house weeping aloud.

events.title: Rebuilding stopped by opposition
events.summary: The people of the land discourage the builders until the reign of Darius.

events.title: Haggai and Zechariah rouse the builders
events.summary: 'Is it a time for you to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?'

events.title: The second Temple completed
events.summary: Finished in the sixth year of Darius and dedicated with joy, seventy years after the first was destroyed.

events.title: Esther becomes queen
events.summary: A Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai is chosen as queen of Persia.

events.title: Haman's plot defeated: the first Purim
events.summary: 'Who knows whether you have not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?' Esther risks her life and her people are saved.

events.title: Ezra returns to teach the Law
events.summary: A scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, who had set his heart to study it, do it, and teach it in Israel.

events.title: Nehemiah rebuilds the walls
events.summary: The king's cupbearer goes to Jerusalem and the walls are rebuilt in fifty-two days, a trowel in one hand and a sword in the other.

events.title: Ezra reads the Law to the people
events.summary: From morning to midday at the Water Gate; the people weep, and are told the joy of the LORD is their strength.

events.title: Nehemiah's second term
events.summary: Back from Persia, he throws Tobiah's furniture out of the Temple and shuts the gates on the Sabbath.

events.title: Fire of Rome; Nero persecutes the Christians
events.summary: Nero blames the Christians for the great fire, and the first imperial persecution begins.

events.title: Peter's martyrdom
events.summary: Crucified at Rome under Nero, by early tradition, as Jesus had told him.

events.title: Paul's last letter and martyrdom
events.summary: 'I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.' Beheaded at Rome, by early tradition.

events.title: Jerusalem and the Temple destroyed by Rome
events.summary: Forty years after Jesus wept over the city, Titus's legions burn the Temple; not one stone is left on another.

events.title: John's Revelation on Patmos
events.summary: Exiled for the word of God, John sees the risen Christ among the lampstands and is told to write what he sees.
